outcome: Quality of vital sign monitoring (frequency of maternal and fetal heart rate, maternal blood pressure, temperature, oxygen saturation, and urine output documentation)
cohort: 360 obstetric admissions at a tertiary care facility in a resource-limited setting
finding: The quality of vital sign monitoring during obstetric hospitalizations was very low, with only a small percentage of women having high-quality monitoring documented.
mod_finding: Women delivering vaginally had higher rates of high-quality monitoring in the first four hours postpartum compared to those delivered by cesarean section (1.4% vs 0%).
